statement: Signs carrying marks on top (roof, antennae or top strokes; no outer or inner marks) sit earlier in texts than their own plain bases, on the holdout. Pairs: all 30 top-only variant-base pairs in the blind annotation data/sign_marks/marks_blind_2026-10-20.csv, classes fixed before computing (results/mark_classes.md): TOP = roof, antennae, top_strokes_*; OUTER = enclosure_strokes, brackets, side_strokes_*; INNER = inner_line, inner_dot, crossbar. Relative position = index/(length-1), texts of 2+ signs. Statistic: base mean relative position minus variant mean, per pair, weighted by variant count over pairs where both occur. Null: variant/base labels permuted within each pair. Exploration: +0.24 (p 0.0005, 547 marked tokens); 10 of 12 marked signs with 4+ uses sit earlier. Caveat: the jar family (G741-G746) and fish family (G235, G240) carry most tokens; Wells (1998, 2006) describes marked jars after the opening cluster G920 G60. Planned support: about 130 marked tokens, from the exploration count and the 80/20 split, not from the holdout; below the project minimum of 15 is reported as below planned support. One-sided. Benjamini-Hochberg across all confirmatory tests.
